newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee futures called flat to 0.50 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee futures called flat to 0.50 lower.

text.p: CSCE arabica coffee futures were called to open unchanged to 0.50 cent lower Thursday as traders expect the market to continue to consolidate after recent sharp gains.

New York coffee futures ended sharply lower in a technical correction Wednesday, with March delivery down 2.90 cents at 144.55 cents a lb after ranging from 148.00 to 144.25. Second-month May finished down 3.35 cents at 139.20 cents, while the outer months fell 3.25 to 3.65.
On the charts, traders pegged support at 143.50-143.25 in the March contract, followed by 142.15. On the upside, 150.00 was seen as strong psychological resistance.
Traders said news Colombian independent coffee growers agreed Wednesday to declare a moratorium on debt payments was likely to have little effect on the futures market.

The moratorium would affect about $200 million in past-due loans owed to the state-run Caja Agria bank and Banco Cafetero, a bank partly owned by the government-affiliated National Coffee Growers' Federation.

Growers also agreed to press for a sharp increase in Colombia's internal coffee price and for government assistance in restructuring their debts. Colombia's internal coffee price was raised 12 percent to 248,1245 pesos per 125-kg load just last week.
London robusta coffee was weaker early Thursday, but above lows. March delivery fell $18 at the midday break to $1,517 a tonne, after sliding to $1,500. May was off $11, to $1,522.
